plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is widely cultivated in gardens, with thousands of cultivars in many forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and Pacific coastal regions
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant (Camellia sinensis), and in Japan its blooms are linked to samurai culture because the whole flower drops at once.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant blossoms on bare branches in the cold of winter, before the leaves emerge. It is a cherished symbol of perseverance and hope in East Asian culture.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated across China, Japan, Korea, and Taiwan
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms appear weeks before cherry blossoms, and the fruit is used to make umeboshi (pickled plums) and umeshu (plum wine).

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking shrub with large, bowl-shaped flower heads made of colorful bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It is adapted to fire-prone, nutrient-poor fynbos soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering from November to February, and some blooms through autumn
plants.location: Native to the southwestern and southern Cape regions of South Africa
plants.funFact: The King Protea is South Africa's national flower, and the genus Protea was named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change shape, because of the plant's great diversity.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes up through snow and frost, heralding the end of winter.
plants.location: Native to Europe from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK, North America, and elsewhere
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.
